name: Nepherites II
summary:
Nepherites II or Nefaarud II was the last pharaoh of the feeble and short-lived Twenty-ninth Dynasty, the penultimate native dynasty of Egypt.

Born into a tumultuous period in Egyptian history, Nepherites II succeeded his brother Psamtik III as ruler around 403 BCE. His reign marked the beginning of the end for the Twenty-ninth Dynasty, which had struggled to maintain power and stability in the face of internal conflicts and external pressures from neighboring kingdoms.

Despite these challenges, Nepherites II implemented several significant reforms aimed at strengthening the Egyptian economy and military. He also launched a series of military campaigns against the Assyrians, who were expanding their empire into Egypt at the time.

Nepherites II's legacy is often overshadowed by that of his more famous predecessors and successors, but his reign provides valuable insights into the complexities of ancient Egyptian politics and society.

The exact circumstances of Nepherites II's death in 379 BCE are unclear, with some sources suggesting he was assassinated by a rival faction within the palace.

As the last native pharaoh of Egypt, Nepherites II's demise marked the beginning of a period of foreign domination that would last for centuries.

The 20th-century discovery of the tomb of Pharaoh Psamtik III in Saqqara provided important archaeological evidence about Nepherites II's life and reign, shedding new light on this enigmatic figure.
